newsitem.title: USA: Perot aide says Dole plea was foolish.
newsitem.headline: Perot aide says Dole plea was foolish.

text.p: Texas billionaire Ross Perot's campaign manager made it clear on Thursday that Perot would not quit the presidential campaign and said Republican Bob Dole's appeal to him to drop out was "absolutely foolish."
The aide, Russ Verney, said on CNN Television that Perot would make his position clear in an address to the National Press Club in Washington later in the day.
"Ross Perot has no intention of withdrawing from this year's election," Verney said.

Dole on Wednesday dispatched his campaign manager Scott Reed to ask Perot to drop out and endorse him. The move was widely viewed as a sign of Dole's desperation less than two weeks before Election Day. President Bill Clinton retains a wide lead in opinion polls.

"This whole effort of first locking Ross Perot out of the debates, pretending that he doesn't exist in American politics...and then in the 11th hour of the campaign, recognising that it is probably the last hope you have to try and win the presidency, for someone to come and ask him to drop out is absolutely foolish. Ross is here to stay," Verney said.
